## Natural history notes

A small owlet moth characterized by mottled brown to grayish-brown forewings with fine wavy lines, darker patches, and a bark-like resting pattern typical of Ptichodis moths. In Florida, it has been recorded as part of the state’s moth fauna and is likely found in warm wooded, shrubby, or semi-open habitats where adults may rest on vegetation or come to lights. Its caterpillar host plants appear to be poorly documented, so it is best treated cautiously as a small nocturnal plant-feeding moth that contributes to the broader food web as prey for spiders, birds, bats, and parasitoid wasps.
